A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AMPO work and provide readable main text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The theoretical analyses, selection code and visualizations can be matched across renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original Llama-3-Instruct alignment results on AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard and MT-Bench, together with temperature/gamma ablations and response-selection visualizations.

after.justification: V2 retains original AMPO evaluations and adds Mistral results, reward-model and response-budget experiments, and the weighting and preference-construction ablations in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The specified training score changes from log P + alpha*(r_i-r_mean) in v1 to log P + alpha*|r_i-r_mean| in v2 Section 3 and Algorithm 1, substantively changing reward weighting beyond the SWEPO-to-REFA terminology change. Appendix B also introduces evaluated uniform versus magnitude-weighted loss variants. The BottomK, Coreset and Opt-Select selection backbone remains.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraFeedback prompts and evaluate the same instruction-following tasks through AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard and MT-Bench. Mistral and the alternative reward model are configuration changes within this retained dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: V1 Table 1 compares AMPO variants with Base and Best-vs-worst (SimPO). V2 retains these and adds reported comparisons with RRHF, SLiC-HF, DPO, IPO, CPO, KTO, ORPO and R-DPO, substantially broadening the comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 adds Mistral-Instruct 7B evaluations, GRM versus Skywork reward-model configurations, negative budgets K=3/5/7, and candidate pools N=16/24/32. Appendix B introduces fixed-budget comparisons of 1-vs-7 versus 4-vs-4 and 1-vs-3 versus 2-vs-2. The original 32-response, temperature-0.8 setup and benchmark metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained temperature, gamma and t-SNE analyses, v2 tests reward-model dependence, negative-set size, candidate-pool size, reward-magnitude weighting and single versus multiple positives. Tables 2–7 provide substantial new evidence about selection efficiency and design choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experimental results. The local-search code's default random seed of 42 is present in both.

E6.justification: V2 adds Mistral, additional-baseline and ablation results. In Table 1, Llama Arena-Hard WR changes from 35.3/39.4/37.9 to 45.2/47.8/46.4 for BottomK/Coreset/Opt-Select, while their AlpacaEval entries remain unchanged. These are revised reported scores; the PDFs do not explain the revisions sufficiently to establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V1's probabilistic multiplicative coreset guarantee is replaced by an additive L*d_max guarantee in v2 Section 7.4 and Theorem E.1. Appendix C changes exponential coverage weights to reward gaps, adds distance-normalization and feasibility assumptions, and replaces the coverage lemma and proof; Appendix E further normalizes the weights. The local-search proof and runtime derivation are also revised, retaining the factor-five claim.

C1.justification: The abstract broadens the AlpacaEval state-of-the-art claim from Llama 8B to Llama 8B and Mistral 7B. The central contributions—active multi-preference selection, expected-reward guarantees and released selection datasets—remain substantially the same.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning reward-model independence, diminishing returns from larger response budgets, reward-calibration sensitivity of magnitude weighting, and reduced ambiguity from using one positive. It also removes v1 Appendix D.1's explicit cautions that the cluster assumptions may fail at high temperatures or be too restrictive in practice.

D1.justification: V2 identifies beta as inverse temperature and documents weighting and fixed-budget construction details for the new ablations. The abstract's dataset-index hyperlink is retargeted, while the two named dataset links remain unchanged. The appendix selection code and its defaults are identical; substantial training and hardware details are still not supplied.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion expands substantially to TRPO/PPO-based RLHF and additional preference-optimization families, including IPO, PRO, rejection sampling, GPO and SLiC-HF. V2 explains more explicitly how REFA addresses MPO/SWEPO limitations and positions AMPO as response selection atop that framework. V1's TDPO discussion and citation are removed.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the introductory motivation and preliminary exposition around budgets and coverage, adds a main-text Related Work section, substantially revises Appendix A and the coreset exposition, removes the separate algorithm walkthrough, and condenses the discussion. SWEPO/REFA terminology and much of the K/N notation are standardized.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, a conceptual Figure 2 is added, Table 1 gains two model blocks and additional comparator rows, and Tables 2–7 are added. Existing sensitivity plots are restyled, the gamma-axis range changes, and experimental takeaways receive shaded boxes. The original main and appendix t-SNE displays are retained as Figures 3 and 6.

improvement.justification: Broader model/baseline comparisons and targeted ablations strengthen v1's narrow empirical support, and the exposition is clearer. However, v2 introduces a mismatch between the reward-gap weights in Appendix C and the exponential weights retained in the main algorithm and code. Opt-Select also has unreconciled MT-Bench entries of 8.0 in Table 1 and 8.11 in several ablation tables. These central consistency problems make the net quality effect uncertain despite the substantial added evidence.
